articles.summary: Tick a layer (Car Paint, Sponsors, Numbers, Tape ...) and the zone only covers pixels that exist on that layer. It is an on/off switch.

Range see SCHEMA: part names come from get_car_map; band 0-1 fractions (height = roof-line to rocker, length = front to rear); rect/cells only for details under ~12% of the sheet, starts at none = 'nothing selected yet'.

controls.label: RESTRICT TO LAYERS
controls.range: see SCHEMA: part names come from get_car_map; band 0-1 fractions (height = roof-line to rocker, length = front to rear); rect/cells only for details under ~12% of the sheet
controls.effect: Tick a layer (Car Paint, Sponsors, Numbers, Tape ...) and the zone only covers...

pitfalls: Layers named Mask / Wire / Car_Mandatory are template layers - do not restrict to them. Unticking everything (All layers) removes the restriction.

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Chooses which pixels the zone owns: a named part (hood, left side), a stripe band, the numbers / sponsors / stripes the app found, a layer, or everything / the rest. Applies to: Where the zone paints.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: It runs over see SCHEMA: part names come from get_car_map; band 0-1 fractions (height = roof-line to rocker, length = front to rear); rect/cells only for details under ~12% of the sheet and starts at none = 'nothing selected yet'. Measured in selection.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: remaining:true = whatever other zones did not claim (keep it last); everything+paintable = whole-car base. exclude:['numbers','sponsors'] keeps decals out. Boxes over ~12% of the sheet are refused.

protips: Typical values: Whole-car look = everything+paintable; a stripe = band; 'only the hood' = part. Put detail zones above the body zone.

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: The zone covers every pixel within tolerance of the picked colour(s) (e.g. 'the red areas'). Applies to: Selects the zone's pixels by their colour in the current paint.

articles.title: Remaining
articles.summary: Makes this zone the catch-all: it gets every pixel no zone above it claims. It is a button.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR. Range 0..n-1 (0 = top).
when: The classic body zone - "everything else".

controls.label: Remaining
controls.effect: Makes this zone the catch-all: it gets every pixel no zone above it claims

pitfalls: Put it at the BOTTOM of the zone list; higher zones win overlaps.

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Where two zones select the same pixel, the LOWER index (higher in the list) wins; the 'remaining' catch-all must be last. Applies to: All zones.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: Behind the scenes it sets the zone position in the zones array. It runs over 0..n-1 (0 = top). Measured in position.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: The zone below only gets pixels the zone above did not claim. A zone that must show on pixels another zone also selects has to sit ABOVE it. priority_override forces a zone to claim before earlier ones.

protips: Typical values: Add detail / accent zones at 'top'; the body base last. If a new zone does not show, it is probably underneath a zone that already claimed those pixels.

faq.q: What does Remaining do?
faq.a: Makes this zone the catch-all: it gets every pixel no zone above it claims.

faq.q: When should I use Remaining?
faq.a: The classic body zone - "everything else".

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of Remaining?
faq.a: Range 0..n-1 (0 = top).

faq.q: Why does Remaining not seem to do what I expect?
faq.a: Put it at the BOTTOM of the zone list; higher zones win overlaps.
